known_open_regression.scope: Research baseline for expired effect-card cleanup; no fix or full-support claim
known_open_regression.observation: A paid Grizzly Bears waits a turn cycle. Paid Fog expires in the original game, whose next-turn declared attack deals two combat damage to take its defender from 40 to 38. The independent copied defender starts at 40, but remains at 40 after its corresponding following-turn combat in both stack-copy modes. Failure occurs after the original expiry and combat assertions pass. Attacker declarations are controlled; subsequent native triggers, blocker decisions and combat damage run natively.

positive_controls: Original paid returns already work. Early moves out of exile and token nonreturn already have the correct visible outcome on both worlds in the baseline, while reporting omitted callbacks. A host gone before its triggered exile resolves already leaves the target unchanged without an unmapped command.

limits: Controlled partial four-player registrations, not full legal-deck games. Eight native scenarios and two identity contracts run both stack-copy modes; two additional paid pending-stack cases run with stack copying enabled.
Ten packaged witnesses pay native spell costs and observe target IDs, zone timestamps, owners/controllers, linked-card membership, mapped worlds and source/copy independence.

Lagrella friendly return counters use fixed legal target choices at the native simultaneous-stack controller boundary. The original controller is restored before copying. The packaged natural AI selects opposing targets; those captures do not prove friendly return counters.
Historical link tests explicitly call cross-game LKI copying and assert canonical mapped target identity and collection independence. They do not certify every historical object subclass.
Early-move and token cases are positive visible-outcome controls. Their baseline diagnostic failures are not described as failed return rules.

The paid pending removal and host-already-gone cases stage explicit stack points. Other settling runs without response priority; arbitrary suspended mid-resolution state and partially accumulated global return-zone tables remain unverified.

Other duration/untap/control deadlines, simultaneous host departures, blink/re-exile incarnation sequences, ownership replacements, hidden/merged/perpetual state and general AI policy require separate implementation or validation.
Other callbacks remain incomplete; unmapped diagnostics are asserted here rather than aggregated into normal simulation reports.

Catalog construction proves script availability, not full gameplay correctness. The seven unavailable entries are nonstarting meld results. Versioned references are not a complete current-rules audit.
